consensus_summary: Primary consensus meaning is the straying sinner (or spiritually lost person/humanity) whom God or Christ the Shepherd actively seeks, finds, and joyfully restores; common alternatives include the specific phrase “lost sheep of the house of Israel,” backslidden believers, and (minority) allegorical or sociorhetorical readings. Scope variations are treated as emphases on the same core image of straying-plus-divine-seeking rather than contradictions.
book_summary: The scattered house of Israel, sought and regathered.
consensus_core_identification: straying sinner / spiritually lost person (or group) sought and restored by the divine Shepherd
book_core_identification: the scattered house of Israel sought and regathered
boundary_disagreement: Consensus primary (and several alternatives) admits any straying sinner, little ones, or backslidden believer; the book restricts the referent exclusively to the national/ethnic house of Israel and excludes the broader individual-sinner cases that dominate the Lukan/Matthean parables.
material_contradiction: None; the book selects and elevates a recognized common alternative without denying the underlying straying-and-seeking motif.
rationale: Minimum cores share the lost-sheep-sought-and-restored category drawn from the same biblical imagery. The book preserves that category but materially narrows its extension to the house of Israel alone (citing the Matthean mission statements), rejecting the consensus primary’s broader application to generic sinners. This is boundary disagreement (REFINED/BOOK_NARROWS/BOOK_SUBSET), not core replacement (DIVERGENT) or absence from consensus (NOVEL).
strongest_objection: The dominant NT parabolic usage (Luke 15; Matt 18) applies the image to individual sinners or vulnerable disciples generally; elevating the Israel-specific phrase to the exclusive meaning may under-weight that primary context.
